newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn says no time limit on EMU stability pact.
newsitem.headline: Bonn says no time limit on EMU stability pact.

text.p: Germany, seeking to push through its demands for a tough stability pact to enforce fiscal discipline under European monetary union, said on Wednesday there was no time limit on agreeing on the pact's terms.
The European Union's monetary committee was meeting in Brussels to try and finalise key points of the pact for review at the EU summit starting on Friday in Dublin.

But, with Germany facing resistance from EU states to its call for only numbers to decide whether a country in recession can exceed the Maastricht treaty's deficit goal, a government spokesman played down expectations of early agreement.

"I expect that a report will be presented on Friday which deals with this theme, and there will be further meetings among the finance ministers. There is no time limit," spokesman Peter Haussmann told a news conference.
"This is a topic which must be discussed further with all seriousness and thoroughness," he added.

Ireland, which holds the rotating EU presidency, is hoping to reach a common position on the pact among member states ahead of the summit. A further meeting of the Ecofin, which groups finance ministers, is planned in Dublin on Thursday.

But, Haussmann pointed out, no final decisions are expected in Dublin, where leaders will review progress on a new EU treaty expected to be completed during the Dutch presidency in the first half of 1997.
